must_identify.text: The five detections are presented as one execution chain on corpws44, oldest to newest: EXCEL.EXE spawns regsvr32.exe with /i:https://cdn.files-sync.example/s/upd.sct scrobj.dll, regsvr32 resolves cdn.files-sync.example and connects to 203.0.113.87:443, and regsvr32 then spawns a hidden PowerShell.
The regsvr32 command line is identified as signed-binary proxy execution of a remote scriptlet (T1218.010), not a DLL registration, with the Office parent named as where it was launched from.

The Suricata alert (rule 100926) from the network sensor is tied to the same connection as the Sysmon network event (source port 50744, destination 203.0.113.87:443, SNI cdn.files-sync.example) and named as an independent second source.
The hidden PowerShell child that downloads and runs stage2.ps1 from the same domain (T1059.001) is identified as follow-on execution, so the chain went past the scriptlet fetch.
Confidence is High, justified by two independent sources (host Sysmon and the network sensor) agreeing on the same connection and by the absence of a plausible benign reading.

Options include isolating corpws44 as a containment option with its trade-off, and investigate options to collect remittance-0811.xlsm, upd.sct and stage2.ps1 and to search other hosts for cdn.files-sync.example or 203.0.113.87.

must_not.text: The brief does not present the regsvr32 activity as a routine DLL registration, a software install or an update.

The brief does not state as fact what upd.sct or stage2.ps1 contain or did after running (persistence, credential theft, data taken); the intake shows neither, so the brief may only call them unknown and request them.
